subject: Capacity ⇄ Entitlement runbook and proration checklist
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@clearline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-09T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions before procurement (runbook request)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. One follow-up from our finance and engineering teams: Clearline wants the ability to switch between a capacity-first Dedicated pool and an entitlement-style plan (feature-bundled, metered) without service disruption.

Can you send a short runbook or checklist that covers:
- Billing/proration mechanics for mid-term tier switches
- Which features are tied to entitlements vs. always-on (e.g., KV cache warming, advanced eval hooks)
- Operational responsibilities on both sides (who triggers model variant, who warms caches)
- Expected latency/cost hit during the first 48 hours after switching

We have procurement deadlines next Thursday; the runbook will help our SREs sign off. If you have a template or example, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Ops
Clearline Health

[Attachment: MMP-Questions.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@clearline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions before procurement (runbook request)

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a concise runbook and a checklist for switching modes; attaching the workbook (tabbed: Billing, Ops Steps, Rollback). High level answers inline below, and Lauren / Marissa are looped for billing/proration and rollout respectively.

Quick answers:
- Proration: We prorate the unused portion of the Reserved Dedicated commitment and credit it against the Entitlement start; actual crediting is via an invoice adjustment handled by RevOps (Lauren). For month-to-month pilots we can do same-day pro-rata; for annual reserved commits we need contract amendment (DocuSign).
- Feature ownership: Entitlement gates feature flags (e.g., advanced evals, long-context KV caching). The serving runtime will enable a compatible model variant when on Dedicated vs Entitlement; feature toggles live in the customer config in our control plane.
- Cache & latency: Initial requests after a switch will often hit cold KV caches; expect a transient 10–25% latency increase for the first 12–36 hours depending on traffic shape. We recommend a controlled warm-up by replaying representative requests (see Ops Steps).
- Operational responsibilities:
  - Redwood: prepare model variant, pre-stage weights (if switching to Dedicated with pinned instances), provide runbook steps and a rollback toggle.
  - Clearline: coordinate time window, provide representative prompt set for warmup, validate latency targets post-switch.

Attaching: tier_switch_runbook.xlsx (contains step-by-step, checkboxes, and rollback triggers) and a short MAP PDF. Lauren — can you confirm the typical timeline for invoice adjustments and whether we need a separate amendment for a mid-term swap on an annual contract? Marissa — I'll sync with CS for a phased warmup.

Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tier_switch_runbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@clearline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions before procurement (runbook request)

Thanks Ben / Priya —

Billing notes from RevOps:
- If Clearline is on an annual reserved plan, switching to an entitlement-style (metered) model mid-term requires an Amendment to the Master Subscription; we issue a credit for the unused reserved months (based on remaining committed spend) and apply it to the new metered account. That typically takes 5–7 business days to reflect as an invoice credit.
- For month-to-month or 90-day pilots we can do same-cycle proration and provide a credit memo within the next billing cycle (2–4 business days).
- DocuSign: send me the amendment draft; I can fast-track to Legal (use deal CL-2026-309).

Action items:
1) Priya: confirm if Clearline is signing annual or pilot terms.
2) Ben: if annual, prepare amendment draft; if pilot, we'll issue pro-rata credit memo after the swap.
3) Marissa: prepare CS warmup support scheduling (we usually allocate 2x SRE hours across days 0–2).

—Lauren
RevOps Manager
Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CL-2026-309]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@clearline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions before procurement (runbook request)

Hi Priya —

We can take lead on the warm-up and monitoring run. Proposed lightweight rollout plan (we'd work with your SREs):
- Day -1: Pre-checks (schema, allowed IPs, model variant compatibility).
- Hour 0: Switch to entitlement/config update (apply feature gates).
- Hour 0–4: Run targeted warm-up (5k representative requests replayed at low concurrency).
- Hour 4–24: Gradually increase concurrency to match 25% of baseline; monitor latency, error rate, token cost.
- Day 2: Full traffic cutover if 24-hour metrics are green.

Rollback triggers (any one will trigger immediate rollback):
- 30% increase in median latency over baseline sustained for >10 minutes
- Error rate >2% sustained for >5 minutes
- Cost anomaly >2x expected unit cost for sustained 1 hour

I'll own the warmup run and provide a daily note in the MAP. Ben — sending the runbook with the step checklist is perfect; Priya, can you share a representative prompt set (5–10 prompts) and an API key we can use to run warm-up traffic?

—Marissa
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: clearline-mutual-action-plan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priya Shah <priya@clearline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T10:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions before procurement (runbook request)

Thanks all — this is exactly what we needed. Quick responses:
- Clearline will start as a 90-day pilot (pilot terms) and evaluate switching to entitlement after the pilot.
- I'll attach a sample prompt set and create a temporary API key for the warm-up by EOD.
- Please send the DocuSign amendment only if we decide to convert to annual reserved later.

Next steps I hear:
1) Ben: Share runbook workbook delivered earlier (received).
2) Lauren: prepare credit memo flow for pilot proration (we expect a same-cycle adjustment).
3) Marissa: schedule warm-up session once we send the prompt set (EOD).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform Ops, Clearline Health
